name: Shaker singing (Shaker hymnody)
lineage: American Shaker (United Society of Believers in Christ's Second Appearing) song tradition, comprising over 10,000 documented hymns composed by Shaker community members in the eighteenth-and-nineteenth-century Shaker communities of New England, New York, Ohio, and Kentucky. Performance: unison-and-octave congregational singing in characteristic strophic-narrative-or-praise form, often associated with the canonical Shaker "labor" of synchronized-rhythmic-walking-and-clapping worship-practice. The 1848 "Simple Gifts" composed by Joseph Brackett at Alfred, Maine became internationally famous after Aaron Copland's 1944 Appalachian Spring incorporation.
